properties.statement: THE KIT MANIFEST CANNOT BE GATED IN CI, AND THAT IS WHY ITS DRIFT SURVIVES. `.reflow2/` is gitignored (.gitignore:22), so `.reflow2/kit-version.json` is NEVER COMMITTED — `git ls-files .reflow2/` returns nothing. A CI checkout therefore has no stamp at all, and any check over it finds nothing to examine and passes. Wiring ver:kit-manifest-agrees into ci.yml would produce a permanently green check that inspects nothing, which is the failure mode this project already names: a green gate is the weakest evidence in the building. FOUND 2026-08-07 while writing that verification, which had sat `planned` since 2026-07-25 — thirteen days in which the stamp went from four releases stale to describing kit 0.22.0/8ed097f against a source at 0.24.0/a5b0f0d. The friction report that raised it said "reflow2's own manifest is four releases stale and nothing noticed"; the reason nothing noticed is structural, not inattention. THE CHECK ITSELF IS WRITTEN AND RUNS (tools/check_kit_manifest.py, 14 cases in tools/test_check_kit_manifest.py), and against this repo it reports exactly one real finding — stale_version — with the ten skill mirrors correctly classified as notes rather than drift. WHERE IT CAN ACTUALLY RUN IS THE OPEN QUESTION, and it is a design question rather than a wiring one: candidates are orientation time (the SessionStart hook already prints an orientation line and already knows whether a design is present), a loop_nudge shape, or folding the hash and file-set claims into `reflow2_init.py --check`, which already reports the VERSION half and is the run people trust before letting anything touch a repo. TWO THINGS THE CHECK GOT WRONG FIRST, both corrected by reading the installer rather than reasoning about it, and both worth keeping as calibration: (1) a manifest entry for a retired file looked like drift and is the installer's INTENDED steady state — install() writes new_manifest[rel] = recorded on purpose at reflow2_init.py:1031 for an edited retired file, so flagging it would make the gate permanently red on any project that ever edited a skill; (2) the six `.claude/skills/` and four `.grok/skills/` copies here are deliberate byte-identical mirrors of getting-started/skills/, enforced by skill_lint (skill_lint.py:45-46), so flagging their mere presence would make the gate red on the one repository that maintains them correctly. A first cut flagged all ten, and a doubled path segment (`skills/skills/...`) made every mirror read as drifted — a path that could not resolve looked identical to a difference.
